lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, soft bass]

[Verse 1: warm, plain, close]
Kettle's cold and the stairs don't creak
Radio's lost the will to speak
The house don't hum
The house don't hum
Since her suitcase hit the street

[Verse 2: strings enter, low and slow]
I wonder where she's laid her head
I wonder if she read what I said
The house don't hum
The house don't hum
There's a hollow in the bed

[Break: band stops except kick and bass, one breath]
And I wait, and I wait, and I wait, and I wait
I wait, I wait, I wait, I wait
I wait, I wait, I wait, I wait
I wait, I wait, I wait, I wait
I ought to go and find her
But I wait

[Verse 3: strings fuller, voice the same]
Clock's still ticking but it's lost its nerve
Dog's at the window, staring at the kerb
The house don't hum
The house don't hum
It's more quiet than I deserve

[Outro: guitar and strings, the title twice, stop]
The house don't hum
The house don't hum
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 78 BPM, 4/4, A minor. Slow, bare and still. A blues without any showing off.

VOICE: Male baritone, warm, plain and conversational, with no vibrato to speak of and no vocal runs. He sings as if talking to himself. In the break he repeats two words rapidly in one long breath, evenly, then delivers the last line slowly.

INSTRUMENTS: A fingerpicked acoustic guitar. A soft, deep electric bass. A string section playing low, sustained, slowly rising lines. A drum kit used very sparingly: a kick and a brushed snare. Nothing else.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and bass. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:38 Verse 2, strings enter. 1:06 Break: everything stops except a kick drum and bass while the two words are repeated, then two slower lines. 1:36 Verse 3, with fuller strings. 2:04 Outro, the title sung twice and a clean stop at 2:25.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1970s soul recorded with a small band: dry, warm and close, a great deal of silence around each sound.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The break at 1:06, sixteen repetitions in one breath.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The lines after the break are the difference: he knows he ought to go and find her, and he waits anyway. It is a more self-aware kind of stuck, and 'more quiet than I deserve' admits some fault.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Emptiness, fixation, a flicker of self-knowledge.
